test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 08 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Choose the correct indirect speech form of the following sentence.

He said, "Will you finish your task on time?"

options.text: He asked me if I should finish my task on time?
He asked me if I should have finished my task on time.
He asked me if I should finish my task on time.
He asked me if I should finish his task on time.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** He asked me if I should finish my task on time.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"Will you finish" becomes "if I should finish"**
 
 
• The modal verb "will" changes to "should" in indirect speech to maintain tense agreement.
 
• Pronoun "you" changes to "I" to match the subject in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Direct speech: "said"
 
• Converted to: "asked" as it is a question.
 
 
 
• **Conjunction:** "if" is used to introduce the indirect question.
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is transformed into a statement without quotation marks.
 
• The question mark is omitted in indirect speech.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He asked me if I should finish my task on time."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "He asked me if I should finish my task on time?" 

 
 
• The question mark is incorrectly used at the end of an indirect speech statement.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "He asked me if I should have finished my task on time." 
 
 
• The use of "should have finished" changes the meaning to a past unreal condition.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "He asked me if I should finish his task on time." 
 
 
• The possessive pronoun "his" is incorrect as the question refers to "my task" in the original sentence.
